citation.title: Effects of repeated bouts versus a single bout of moderate-intensity exercise on postexercise cognitive inhibitory control

population.description: Twenty healthy, recreationally active young men, age 21.0 ± 0.4 years (mean ± SEM; SD computed as 0.4 x sqrt(20) = 1.79), body weight 64.0 ± 2.0 kg, height 172.6 ± 0.7 cm, VO2peak 45.9 ± 1.0 mL/kg/min; BMI not printed. Crossover, same men in both arms. VO2peak (ramp-incremental cycle test; Methods, Participants: 'VO2 peak: 45.9 +/- 1.0 ml min-1 kg-1', mean +/- SEM; SD = 1.0 x sqrt(20) = 4.47).

protocols.name: rex
protocols.description: Cycle ergometer, two 20-min bouts at 60% VO2peak separated by a 20-min seated rest (R-EX): bouts at minutes 0 to 20 and 40 to 60. Activity level is derived, not stated: 60% of the group's mean VO2peak 45.9 mL/kg/min (Methods, Participants; ramp test on the cycle ergometer) = 27.54 mL/kg/min; level = (27.54 - 3.7) / 31.7 = 0.7521. Fasted: the men abstained from food, caffeine and alcohol for 12 h before each experiment (stated); nothing eaten or given during the session is reported, so no meals. Clock hour of day not printed (8.0 assumed). Time axis: minute 0 is the pre-exercise sample (taken after 5 min seated rest, immediately before the pre-exercise Stroop test, whose duration is not printed and is ignored), and both arms have the same 60 min from there to the end of exercise (the paper gives S-EX its 20 min rest so that the intervals between Stroop tests match). The immediate post-exercise sample is taken immediately before the first post-exercise Stroop test, with heart rate still at exercise level, so it is entered at minute 59, the last minute of exercise, so that the input is still on; the 10, 20 and 30 min post-exercise samples are minutes 70, 80, 90.
